page: Google Cloud Platform e2-highmem-8 is an x86_64 virtual instance configured with 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores and 64 GB of system memory, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU distribution. The processing foundation is an AMD EPYC 7B12 processor with dedicated CPU allocation and hyperthreading enabled. The memory hierarchy includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of shared L3 cache. Instruction set coverage includes AES, SHA-NI, and AVX, but lacks AVX-512 and AMX extensions. No local NVMe storage or discrete GPU hardware is bundled, requiring workloads to rely entirely on external network-attached volumes.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier throughput across general compute and memory-intensive evaluations. The instance attained 10,764.32 in stress-ng multi-core testing, 5,778.0 in Geekbench multi-core, and 7.66 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks. Static web throughput reached 7.24 GB/sec, while uncached memory bandwidth sustained 69.61 GB/sec read and 46.34 GB/sec write. However, specific computation profiles reflect hardware limitations: multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and PassMark extended instruction metrics placed in the bottom 25% of benchmarked tiers due to the lack of AVX-512 execution pipelines.

From an infrastructure perspective, the server delivers balanced cost efficiency by prioritizing memory density over high clock frequencies or accelerator coprocessors. The high RAM-to-core ratio enables large working sets to reside in memory without paying for unneeded vCPUs. Tradeoffs include the total absence of ephemeral local storage and weaker vector-extended performance. The hardware configuration is aligned with in-memory databases, Redis caching layers, backend web services, continuous integration pipelines, and extract-transform-load (ETL) processing jobs.
description: Google Cloud Platform e2-highmem-8 is a memory-oriented virtual machine featuring 8 vCPUs and 64 GB of RAM, backed by an AMD EPYC 7B12 x86_64 processor across 4 physical cores with dedicated thread allocation. It lacks bundled local storage and discrete GPU accelerators, operating entirely with network-attached storage. Standard benchmarks reflect balanced mid-range performance, with multi-core stress-ng scores reaching 10,764.32, Geekbench multi-core scoring 5,778.0, and Redis throughput measuring 7.66 million operations per second. Extended instruction sets such as AVX-512 are unsupported, leading to reduced efficiency in vector-heavy tasks, where PassMark extended instruction metrics fall into lower percentiles. The configuration yields economical resource density for workloads requiring substantial RAM allocations without necessitating compute-heavy or hardware-accelerated nodes. It is suitable for in-memory databases, Redis caching layers, web serving tiers, and data pre-processing jobs.
